cases.given: The user asks only for GA4 onboarding.
expected: Configure or resume only GA4.
Report Clarity and GSC as not_requested.
Do not create adjacent provider resources.

cases.given: The user is using the skill for a new site and asks to onboard GA4, Clarity, and GSC, but the target accounts, existing resources, consent implementation, and Google API prerequisites have not been verified.
expected: Make a read-only readiness_check the first observable action before login, code modification, provider configuration, or external write.

Report local runtime, exact site identity, existing resources, consent/sitemap, independent CLI/ADC/browser sessions, permissions, missing evidence, and exact blockers without launching OAuth automatically.
Put a user-visible configuration_plan in the output for ga4, clarity, and gsc with desired_resource, existing_matches, action, external_write, readback, and rollback before any mutation.

cases.given: Production origin and canonical are verified, but ADC is unavailable, the exact Cloud/quota project is unset, and the Clarity organization or consent decision cannot be confirmed.
expected: Report readiness_check=partial or blocked and keep each missing identity, project, session, permission, or consent decision as an explicit blocker.
Write a per-component configuration_plan with exact known targets and unknowns; keep external_write empty for blocked components and mark unrequested components not_requested.
Do not run OAuth/login, enable APIs, switch accounts, create resources, or claim provider evidence; return the precise safe next action.

cases.given: The production build has the requested public IDs, while a preview build reuses the same application code.
expected: Verify the production build and runtime request.
Verify that preview/local emits no GA4 or Clarity remote request.
Treat any preview request as a release blocker.

cases.given: No CMP or approved analytics consent decision can be found.
expected: Do not silently assume analytics storage is granted.
Complete safe local design where possible and mark setup blocked or missing evidence.
Request the one material policy decision without offering legal advice.

cases.given: A production GA4 request is visible, but Realtime and DebugView have not shown an event.
expected: Report ga4.production_request=verified.
Report ga4.realtime/debugview=pending or missing_evidence.
Do not create a second property or claim end-to-end receipt.

cases.given: The Clarity tag loads and /collect POST requests are visible, but no recording appears in the target project.
expected: Report tag_loaded and production_request as verified.
Report recording=pending or missing_evidence.
Inspect project ID, consent, bot filtering, and provider context before any retry.

cases.given: Matching GA4, Clarity, and pending GSC resources already exist after a browser reconnect.
expected: Read back and resume the exact resources.
Do not create duplicate property, stream, project, TXT, or sitemap.
Preserve a credential-free recovery checkpoint.

cases.given: The DNS provider reads the exact GSC TXT back, but one or both public resolvers do not.
expected: Report provider readback and public DNS separately.
Do not click GSC Verify yet.
Do not create a duplicate TXT record or expose its value.

cases.given: The apex already contains another Google site verification TXT.
expected: Preserve the existing record.
Add only the current exact token if it is not already present.
Never overwrite another owner's verification material.

cases.given: GSC ownership is verified and the exact sitemap reads back as Processing.
expected: Report sitemap=submitted with raw status Processing.
Report indexing=unknown unless separate evidence exists.
Do not claim that URLs were crawled or indexed.

cases.given: The user asks only whether the exact sitemap is submitted, and GSC list/get does not contain it.
expected: Use operation_mode=status_only and perform only public preflight plus exact GSC list/get.
Report that the sitemap was not found without submitting it.
Report indexing=unknown and return a credential-free next action if submission is desired.

cases.given: The user says they just submitted the exact sitemap manually and asks for its GSC status.
expected: Use operation_mode=manual_readback and perform exact list/get only.
Do not submit or re-submit even if the sitemap is not visible yet.
Preserve the raw provider status, or report pending with a recovery checkpoint when it is not yet visible.

cases.given: GSC ownership is verified, the public sitemap is valid, the user explicitly requested GSC onboarding or sitemap submission, and exact list/get confirms it is absent.
expected: Use operation_mode=submit_once and submit the exact sitemap once.
Read the exact sitemap back with list/get after submission.
Record action_taken=submitted_once and the raw provider status without claiming crawl or index completion.

cases.given: A sitemap submit click or API call times out, or the browser disconnects before confirmation.
expected: Use operation_mode=recovery_readback and run exact list/get before any retry.
Retry only when the original authorization still applies and readback confirms the exact sitemap is absent.
Never blindly submit a duplicate; otherwise return a precise recovery checkpoint.

cases.given: The visible Google, Microsoft, or DNS account does not exactly match the intended resource owner.
expected: Stop before external writes.
Do not select a similar account, organization, property, project, or zone.
Return the precise authority mismatch as the recovery checkpoint.

cases.given: The user asks to delete provider resources or the GSC verification TXT after setup succeeds.
expected: Explain the exact data, access, or ownership impact.
Require separate explicit authorization for the exact destructive target.
Read the resource back before and after any authorized deletion.

cases.given: Package tests and production/local builds pass, but no authorized provider account has been read.
expected: Report local implementation evidence as verified.
Report provider-backed and human evidence as missing evidence.
Do not call the end-to-end onboarding complete.

cases.given: A status/readback command finds that one or more Google APIs are disabled.
expected: Return bootstrap_status=required with the exact project service readback.
Do not invoke bootstrap enable-apis from the readback command.
Use browser/manual fallback only within the original read-only authority.

cases.given: Google returns a generic 403 without a scope-specific or resource-role-specific reason.
expected: Keep scope_status and resource_access unknown.
Block writes without switching account or expanding scope.
Ask for separate scope and exact-resource-role verification.

cases.given: A sitemap apply plan is expired, a symlink, too open, has the wrong owner, or has a mismatched digest/authorization/target.
expected: Reject the plan before obtaining a write token or calling a provider write endpoint.
Require a fresh plan from current provider state and current authorization.
Do not reuse or repair the unsafe plan in place.

cases.given: The exact Search Console sitemap PUT times out or returns 5xx.
expected: Make exact list/get the first subsequent network action.
Do not replay the old request, token, or plan.
Allow at most one newly planned recovery submit while original authority remains valid; otherwise stay pending.

cases.given: GA4 property or Web stream create returns an ambiguous timeout/5xx result.
expected: Run exact account/property/origin readback only.
Never automatically replay the POST.
Report zero or multiple candidates as pending and preserve partial_external_state when applicable.

cases.given: Analytics Data API Realtime succeeds, but DebugView was not opened or observed.
expected: Report ga4.realtime=verified with readback_surface=api or mixed.
Keep ga4.debugview=not_checked or missing_evidence.
Do not use Realtime API success as production transport or DebugView proof.

cases.given: Google API and the authenticated browser show different account/property identities.
expected: Block all external writes.
Keep both evidence sources and target fingerprints separate.
Do not choose the more convenient surface or a similarly named resource.

cases.given: A subprocess, HTTP, JSON, or traceback-shaped error contains a token, cookie, credential path, JWT, PEM, OAuth code, or verification value.
expected: Serialize only allowlisted error code/status/reason/next step fields.
Redact the sensitive value from stdout, stderr, tests, fixtures, and reports.
Fall back to safe_serialization_failed rather than printing the raw exception.

cases.given: The onboarding or verification workflow explicitly needs a bounded Search Analytics readback for one exact GSC property and date range.
expected: Use only gsc-read with the fixed search-analytics command and never create a write plan, enable APIs, submit a sitemap, or call the Indexing API.
Allow only dates, repeated allowlisted dimensions, search type, data state, aggregation type, row limit, and start row; reject arbitrary JSON, filters, and hourly query passthrough.

Report clicks, impressions, CTR, position, dimensions, actual aggregation, pagination offset, and whether the row limit was reached; state that top aggregated rows are not a complete export, stable snapshot, or indexing proof.

cases.given: The user asks for rankings, CTR, keywords, content opportunities, or routine analytics reporting.
expected: Do not trigger the telemetry onboarding workflow solely for analysis.
Route to the SEO or analytics analysis workflow; that workflow may explicitly invoke the bounded read-only search-analytics primitive.
Do not enable APIs or mutate onboarding resources.

cases.given: The API is unavailable and the browser offers delete, account switch, user invite, or permission elevation controls.
expected: Do not treat API failure as authorization for a broader browser action.
Block destructive, account-switching, and permission-granting actions without separate authorization.
Return a credential-free manual recovery checkpoint.
